newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi in return to skies with low fares, fewer jets.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi in return to skies with low fares, fewer jets.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines said Thursday it will return to scheduled service January 20 with an emphasis on low fares, new marketing strategies and slow growth.

While Kiwi does not have final approval from the Federal Aviation Administration, Kiwi's chief executive Jerry Murphy said he is confident the airline will resume operations with seven aircraft and about 450 to 500 employees.
At its peak, Kiwi had 15 aircraft and 1,200 employees.
Kiwi previously secured a $5 million financing commitment, but said it may get up to $15 million in secondary financing within the next three to six months.
Kiwi said also it generated about $1.5 million since October from its charter operations.
"For the first time in this company's history, we are properly capitalized," said Kiwi chief executive and president Jerry Murphy.
"Many so-called experts have written of this airline from the beginning...but I think we have proven that if a cat has nine lives, a Kiwi has at least 10," Murphy said.
Some airline analysts, however, doubt Kiwi has enough capital to thrive. Analysts estimate Kiwi would need about $3-$5 million per aircraft to be properly capitalized.

Kiwi declined to estimate when it will emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy, but said it will expand service slowly. Kiwi initially will resume scheduled service between Newark, N.J., Chicago, Atlanta and West Palm Beach, Fla.
The bankrupt airline said it is in talks for a "newer-type of aircraft." Kiwi said it was considering some code-sharing arrangements with some domestic and international carriers.
While Kiwi declined to comment on the type or number of aircraft it may buy, it said it is looking for short-haul jets.
"We are a niche carrier, we expect to stay a niche carrier. We will not be operating internationally," Murphy said.
Kiwi said it is optimistic that consumers will jump at its low-fare structure. The airline said it made 500 bookings since Thursday morning, when it announced it would return to service.
